title: Phase-aware burst allocator and hedged-prefill policy to balance latency vs throughput
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Goal: design and prototype a phase-aware burst allocator combined with a hedged-prefill policy that reduces p95/p99 tail latency for interactive decode-heavy workloads while preserving steady-state throughput and fair token allocation across tenants.

Background: current prefill/decode scheduler groups tokens into coarse prefill and decode phases. Under spiky arrival patterns (e.g., interactive chat bursts), long prefill queues can push up tail latency for small low-latency requests and for high-priority customers. Existing phase-splitting work reduces some contention but lacks dynamic burst sizing, tenant-weight fairness, and hedged-prefill hedging to protect against stragglers.

Proposed solution: implement a Burst Allocator micro-policy layered on the arbitration queue with three components: 1) Phase Alignment Windowing: split incoming prefill tokens into phase-aligned bursts sized by recent per-tenant inter-arrival patterns (exponential moving average of burst length). Bursts are constrained by max_burst_tokens and min_burst_tokens config flags. 2) Soft QoS Weights: allocate burst slots to tenants using a weighted deficit-round-robin where weight = tenant_token_share * urgency_multiplier. Urgency multiplier is derived from SLA label + short-term latency debt. 3) Hedged-prefill: for requests predicted to be latency-sensitive (short decode expected), issue a small hedged prefill to a warm worker after a hedge-delay threshold. Hedged prefill uses a compact KV-cache hint to avoid full duplicate compute. If the hedge returns earlier, we cancel the original long prefill decode and prefer the hedged result.

Trade-offs and safeguards: hedging reduces tail latency at the cost of extra compute; we bound hedging by a global hedged_tokens_budget and per-tenant hedging_quota. Burst sizing favors latency for small interactive sessions and favors throughput for background bulk workloads by tuning the burst_sensitivity parameter per project.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (spike): implement burst allocator library in runtime scheduler with an opt-in flag. Add metrics and tracing for burst events. (2 wks)
- Phase 2 (experiment): enable hedged-prefill on an internal canary for 10% of traffic on dedicated pools; collect p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, and hedged-hit/cancel rates. (2 wks)
- Phase 3 (rollout): iterate thresholds and weights, add tenant-level config via console, and document operational runbooks. (1–2 wks)

Measurement: success criteria include: 25–40% reduction in p99 latency for interactive workload samples, <=5% regression on tokens/sec throughput in dedicated pools, hedged prefills account for <7% of total tokens consumed and have >70% early-hit cancellation.

Operational hooks: dashboard cards for burst-size distribution, hedged_cancellations, per-tenant latency debt, and cost-impact. Feature gated behind runtime-1.20 and per-pool capability flags.
acceptance_criteria: Burst allocator library merged behind feature flag and unit tested
Canary experiment shows >=25% p99 latency reduction on interactive sample with <=5% throughput regression
Tenant-weighting prevents starvation: no tenant p95 increase >10% in experiment window
Hedged-prefill budget controls and cancellation metrics present in Console dashboard
Runbook written: how to disable hedging, adjust burst_sensitivity, and emergency rollback steps
